requirements.statement: The Alphazedehq repository shall contain one shared skill `skills/spec-authoring/` holding a `SKILL.md` within skill_size_max, a specification template, and build, lint and diagram scripts that run with `uv run --script` (PEP 723 inline dependencies) and Graphviz `dot`, without any project-specific Python environment, and shall retain the GridMarket MIT copyright and permission notice.

The spec-authoring skill’s operational text, templates and tool invocation shall contain no GridMarket product name, document id or `--project backend` flag; GridMarket references shall occur only in retained license, attribution and provenance records, and the skill shall contain no absolute local path; building and linting its shipped template in a temporary directory outside any git repository shall exit 0.

The spec-authoring skill description shall name SDoc and Requirements System documents as non-triggers and shall cite `requirements-engineering` by reference without restating its checklist, so that a request to author and build a Markdown specification selects spec-authoring and a request to publish an SDoc revision to the Requirements System selects `use-requirements-system`.

The skill’s vendor step shall copy its scripts to `<repo>/tools/spec/` with a `VENDORED.md` naming the source repository, commit and MIT notice, and shall refuse to overwrite a vendored copy whose files differ from that recorded commit.

The program shall land the spec-authoring skill in Alphazedehq through its own pull request merged by rebase or merge commit, shall then link it into every harness skill directory that already links the shared skills, and shall have the D4 hook installer link it for the remaining harnesses of SD-021 or record each as a typed gap.

requirements.allocation: S06 (PR), S06L (links), S11 (Muse/AGY links or typed gaps)

requirements.statement: The shared `setup-pre-commit` skill shall define one repo-agnostic gate entrypoint contract, shall ship a template gate script and an installer for local git hooks that invoke it, shall state that GitHub Actions invoke the same entrypoint, shall contain no `[TODO]` text, and its `SKILL.md` shall be within skill_size_max.

The shared `setup-a-repo` skill shall reference a workflow-authoring guide stating the rules of AC-AFC-CI-02 plus free hosted runners on public repositories and the gh_private_minutes budget (C11), and shall ship a checker script that exits non-zero on a workflow violating any of those rules; its `SKILL.md` shall be within skill_size_max.

The shared `ship-pull-request` skill shall run `vnv-review` when the repository has a Vnv guidance tree (`docs/vnv/AGENTS.md` or `Vnv/AGENTS.md`) and otherwise record REFUSED_NO_VNV, never a pass; its `references/GATES.md` shall gain a shared-gate row and an amazon-fantasy-companion row; its `SKILL.md` shall be within skill_size_max.

When AC-AFC-D4-01..03 are merged (C13), one shared hook script shall run the current repository’s gate entrypoint before an agent-initiated `git commit` or `git push` in every harness named in SD-021 that exposes a pre-tool hook; the installer shall record each harness without one as a typed gap with its exact evidence, and shall expose the D4 skills in Muse’s skill directory.

risks.risk: A frozen route’s usage window runs out mid-wave (observed: Muse HTTP 429 on 2026-10-11, reset 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z).
risks.control: If a selected route reaches a confirmed usage or rate limit, then the Orchestrator shall record the limit evidence and activate only the next approved fallback in the frozen profile with a class B receipt preserving the selected coverage-assist and Reverify settings, or queue the slice when no approved fallback remains; other invocation, configuration, authentication or runtime errors shall not trigger a route switch.
risks.recovery: Activate the next approved fallback; queue the slice when all are exhausted.

risks.risk: Actions minutes on the private repository run out (C11).
risks.control: If private-repository Actions usage exhausts gh_private_minutes, then the program shall stop hosted workflow runs and retain local gate evidence without enabling paid overage unless the owner authorizes it.
risks.recovery: Hosted runs stop; local gate evidence continues; no paid overage without the owner.

risks.risk: A secret, account detail or absolute local path reaches the public repository.
risks.control: When a secret, personal account detail or absolute local path is detected in material intended for the public repository, the program shall block its merge or publication until sanitized; if exposure has already occurred, it shall record the affected artifact without reproducing the sensitive value and notify the owner for credential rotation or other protected remediation.
risks.recovery: Remove before merge; credential rotation is the owner’s action.

risks.risk: Muse or AGY exposes no pre-tool hook surface.
risks.control: If Muse or AGY exposes no supported pre-tool hook, then the D4 installer shall record that harness as a typed gap with exact capability evidence and retain local git hooks invoking the shared gate, without treating those hooks as proof of the missing harness integration.
risks.recovery: Record the gap; git hooks still run the gate locally.

risks.risk: Imported software or a pinned action is compromised.
risks.control: The program shall obtain a scan-software-supply-chain receipt before first use of each external software acquisition (uv, Graphviz, the GridMarket source at its pinned commit, each pinned GitHub Action), and refuse use on BLOCK or INDETERMINATE.
risks.recovery: Fail closed on BLOCK or INDETERMINATE.

risks.risk: Both skills trigger on “architecture specification” requests.
risks.control: If matching and non-matching request checks expose a trigger collision between the D5 skill and `use-requirements-system`, then the program shall record the failing requests and repair the D5 trigger boundary under AC-AFC-D5-03; any reciprocal edit to `use-requirements-system` shall follow the OD-AFC-07 disposition recorded at integrated review.
risks.recovery: Narrow the descriptions in the D5 repair round; never merge two skills.

risks.risk: D5 lands late and delays D1.
risks.control: If D5 lands later than planned, then spec-track D1 assembly (ST-4) shall wait for the D5 merge and the S42 vendoring, the spec-track entry receipt shall record the slip, and the program shall not revert to the superseded project-local GridMarket kit; spec-track requirements and model work (ST-2, ST-3) shall continue.
risks.recovery: D1 waits; register and model work proceeds; no fallback to copying the GridMarket kit.

risks.risk: Spec-first moves product implementation later; the deadline is fixed. Moving all product slices out of Phase 1 also drops the f885e48 plan to capture ESPN fixtures from the Monday 2026-10-12 US game.
risks.control: When the Phase 2 plan is approved (P2-6), it shall state the remaining days to T_deadline and the live NFL windows still available, and shall present any scope reduction as an owner decision at the Phase 2 integrated review rather than cutting scope silently.
risks.recovery: Spec-track requirements and model work start at approval in parallel with the D5/D4 waves; the Phase 2 plan re-plans spikes and fixture capture against the remaining windows (Thu 10-15, Sun 10-18, Mon 10-19, Thu 10-22 US time); owner decides cuts.

D4 form: extend the existing shared skills only (SD-018), or extend them and add one thin shared entry-point skill (the owner’s latest words were “Just create the shared skill please”). Recommendation: **A — extensions only.** `setup-pre-commit` becomes the shared CI/CD gate skill and is already linked into every harness. A second entry-point skill would only route to the three extended skills and duplicate their trigger surface, which C10 forbids. If “the shared skill” meant one new named skill, option B costs one judgement slice (S41, `skills/ci-cd/SKILL.md`, a router under 25 lines) and changes nothing else.

.gitignore `*.log` hides specialist logs that are cited as evidence. Recommendation: Add a negation for `docs/plans/**/specialists/*.log` in the planning commit so the evidence is tracked (SD-011), after the Orchestrator scrubs absolute local paths.

D5 trigger boundary: add the reciprocal non-trigger to `use-requirements-system`’s description in the same D5 pull request? Recommendation: Yes. Today both descriptions match “write the architecture specification”. One line in each removes the collision (RISK-AFC-15). Without it, S06 edits only the new skill and records the remaining collision.

D5 shape: one skill `spec-authoring` (figure and lint detail in `references/`), or three skills mirroring GridMarket. Recommendation: One skill. The three share one trigger surface and one toolchain (C10).

Vendor the D5 scripts into this repository’s `tools/spec/` so public CI can run the `spec` area, given that Alphazedehq is private (S42). Recommendation: Yes. The scripts derive from public MIT code. SD-011 already makes this repository public. The MIT notice travels in `VENDORED.md` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

In a repository without a Vnv guidance tree, does `ship-pull-request`’s `REFUSED_NO_VNV` block the merge? Recommendation: No. Record it as a non-pass gate row (C12) and let the repository’s required checks decide. Blocking would stop merges in every repository the owner touches (SD-019). This repository has a tree, so it always runs `vnv-review`.

Lane for the D4/D5 skill-authoring slices (S01, S02, S03, S06). **A:** spec-and-docs = tech-writing profile (single_implementer; Reviewer with OCR still applies). **B:** keep SKILL.md and references text on tech-writing, and move the executable parts (gate template, hook installer, workflow checker, D5 scripts) to the primary profile with tdd. Recommendation: **A** for the schedule. B’s risk stays visible: the executable shared tooling gets no Assurance Test Engineer pass, only the Reviewer and the scripts’ own tests. Phase 1 has more slack than f885e48 had, so B is now affordable: it costs about one day and a slice-graph/SEIT regeneration.

Review cadence boundary in Phase 1 (IE-P1-F01). The frozen profiles say Reviewer cadence `phase`, and Phase 1 is one phase. Wave 2 needs Wave 1 pull requests merged, and merging needs the review. So a single end-of-phase review deadlocks. **A:** keep `cadence: phase` and treat each integration step IE-P1-1..IE-P1-11 as Phase 1’s review boundary, so each pull request is reviewed once at its own step. **B:** an owner amendment of the frozen cadence to `slice` for Phase 1. Recommendation: **A.** The review count is the same as one review per pull request at phase end (13 or fewer), only earlier, and the frozen profile is unchanged. If the owner reads A as a cadence change, B records it explicitly; nothing else in the plan changes.

dispatch_records.convention: Every slice dispatch, first or repeated, has one dispatch record. The Orchestrator writes it into journey.json execution_receipts (kind `dispatch_record`) before the dispatch and names it in the packet. A packet without its dispatch record is an Orchestrator defect; the implementer returns CONTRACT_FAILURE before any edit (S01 Wave 1 re-dispatch finding).
dispatch_records.when: Before each dispatch. A re-dispatch increments generation and writes a new record; the record releases the previous generation's lease.

fields.lease_id: <slice>-g<generation>, for example S01-g3. Generation counts every dispatch of that slice in this Lifecycle, earlier rounds included (S01 Wave 1 = g1, re-dispatch = g2).

fields.base: full SHA the worktree was created from; it is <base> in CMD-D4-AGNOSTIC and CMD-D5-AGNOSTIC
